posts.title: The Cpu Works Somehow
posts.description: You can create a simple CPU by using a bunch of transistors to build logic gates (AND, OR, NAND, etc.), then connecting those gates so they run actual logic and computations. However, I could not understand how such simple primitives could perform fairly complicated operations in a very small number of machine cycles - sometimes even in a single cycle. Confusion I will use addition as an example.
